name: The Cemetery Complexes of the Xiongnu Nobility
description: Eight burial grounds scattered across the Mongolian steppe hold the graves of the Xiongnu elite, rulers of a nomadic empire that rivalled Han China more than 2,000 years ago. Each complex centres on a large, deep tomb ringed by small round satellite mounds and lines of paired stones used for offerings. Chariots, horse gear, weapons and food left for the afterlife reveal how these horsemen lived and organised their society.
